HOW IT HAPPENED: THE FAULT CHAIN
Cause → mechanism → fault. Every link shows the evidence it rests on and how sure we are.

text.tspan: Not measurable directly. Pointed to by: lead hip turned
Measured: hips moved toward the ball by 7% of body

svg.text: hips toward the ball, address → impact

text.tspan: Verified: early extension. The rule table decides; the AI
Your hips moved toward the ball on the way down: 7% of your body height between address and impact.
That crowds your arms, so your body stands up to make room. That is early extension. The likely
reason is that your hips are not turning enough. At impact your lead hip had turned 31°, where we
typically see around 45°. When the hips cannot turn out of the way, they move forward instead. It may
feel like you stay down, but at impact your hips have moved toward the ball. For the rest of this bucket,
do the wall drill: it lets you feel the hips turning back instead of forward. Add the 90/90 hip rotation at
home to free up the turn.

Why does it feel like I’m staying down when I’m not?
Your upper body keeps its bend, so it feels like you stay down.
But your hips moved toward the ball by 7% of your body height
between address and impact (the threshold is 4%). To make room
for your arms, you stand up through the ball.
